evidence: src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp is the only place that builds the repositories, StockReservationService, use cases and controllers, and it mounts them along with errorHandlerMiddleware.
src/infrastructure/error-handler-middleware.ts: STATUS_BY_KIND is the only mapping from DomainErrorKind to HTTP status. No controller sets error statuses itself.

src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts: OrderController uses the injected use cases, throws InvalidRequestError and reuses the domain's isOrderState. TRANSITION_ACTIONS only maps URL actions to states and leaves transition validity to TransitionOrderUseCase.
src/infrastructure/stock-controller.ts: StockController follows the same constructor-injected use case plus routes(): Router pattern as OrderController.
src/infrastructure/in-memory-order-repository.ts and src/infrastructure/in-memory-product-repository.ts implement the OrderRepository and ProductRepository ports with the same Map-backed approach.
src/infrastructure/uuid-id-generator.ts: UuidIdGenerator implements the domain IdGenerator port.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only seeds the catalogue and calls createApp(...).listen.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/infrastructure module is one coherent unit. It holds the adapters and the composition root for the hexagonal design:
- HTTP adapters: OrderController, StockController and errorHandlerMiddleware.
- Persistence adapters: InMemoryOrderRepository and InMemoryProductRepository, which implement the domain repository ports.
- An id adapter: UuidIdGenerator, which implements IdGenerator.
- Wiring: createApp in app.ts and the entry point in server.ts.

The files use their abstractions consistently. Both controllers depend only on injected use cases and expose routes(): Router. Both repositories implement domain ports in the same Map-backed style. Validation failures throw the domain's InvalidRequestError, and one place, STATUS_BY_KIND in error-handler-middleware.ts, turns errors into HTTP status codes. The order-state check reuses the domain's isOrderState instead of copying it. No file bypasses the module's own abstractions: app.ts wires everything through constructors.

TRANSITION_ACTIONS in order-controller.ts only maps HTTP action names to target states. It does not repeat the transition rules, which TransitionOrderUseCase still enforces. Mixing HTTP and persistence adapters in one infrastructure module is the usual adapter-layer shape, not a split into unrelated concerns.
